Consider the finite region bounded by the curves $x=7-y-{y}^{2},$ $x=5-{y}^{2},$ and the $x$-axis, as shown above. Calculate the volume $V$ of the solid generated when this region is rotated $2\pi $ radians about the $x$-axis. Do not round the answer.

$V=$
{{field-1}}
question.worked_solution:
Now, let $f(y)=7-y-{y}^{2}$ and $g(y)=5-{y}^{2}.$

We start by determining the points where the curves intersect by solving the following equation for $y:$

$$
\begin{aligned}f(y) & =g(y) \\ 7-y-{y}^{2} & =5-{y}^{2} \\ 2-y & =0 \\ y & =2\end{aligned}
$$

The solution corresponding to our region is $y=2.$ So, we need to integrate from $y=0$ to $y=2.$ 

Now, let's draw our usual horizontal arrow through the region to determine the left and right functions.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14224622/assets/cfb914bf7ed0a0c6b9f784d46a6761cd97c352fcc4e82abb29a72dc12d8ab7ca.png)

The horizontal arrow 

- *enters* the region through the left function $x=g(y)=5-{y}^{2},$ and

- *leaves* through the right function $x=f(y)=7-y-{y}^{2}.$

Therefore, using the shell method, the volume of the solid can be found as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}V & =2\pi {\int }_{c}^{d}y([\text{right}]-[\text{left}])\,\text{d}y \\  & =2\pi {\int }_{0}^{2}y([7-y-{y}^{2}]-[5-{y}^{2}])\text{d}y \\  & =2\pi {\int }_{0}^{2}y(2-y)\text{d}y \\  & =2\pi {\int }_{0}^{2}(2y-{y}^{2})\text{d}y \\  & =2\pi (2{\int }_{0}^{2}y\,\text{d}y-{\int }_{0}^{2}{y}^{2}\text{d}y) \\  & =2\pi ({2\cdot \frac{{y}^{2}}{2}|}_{0}^{2}-{\frac{{y}^{3}}{3}|}_{0}^{2}) \\  & =2\pi (2(\frac{4}{2}-0)-(\frac{8}{3}-0)) \\  & =2\pi (4-\frac{8}{3}) \\  & =2\pi \cdot \frac{4}{3} \\  & =\frac{8\pi }{3}\end{aligned}
$$
